title: Reserved Capacity Negotiation Playbook - QA Draft
content:
Purpose: quick reference and scripted nudges for AE/SE when negotiating Reserved Capacity (Dedicated) commitments. Focus: preserve margin, limit contractual risk, give clear fallback offers and time-boxed concessions.

Audience: Account Execs, Solutions Engineers, Sales Ops, GTM Leadership.

High-level negotiation objectives:
- Anchor on throughput and predictable unit economics rather than raw GPU count.
- Preserve minimum viable discount tiers (tier 1: <12 months, tier 2: 12-24, tier 3: 24+).
- Limit long-term model/architecture guarantees; offer operational SLOs and rollback/fallbacks instead.
- Keep legal redlines minimal: avoid open-ended indemnities, limit data residency exceptions to Private product line.

Quick math (talk track examples):
- Baseline: hosted list rates = $0.024 / 1k tokens (generation), $0.12 / 1k vectors (embedding) (example only).
- Mid-market reserved offer: 40% discount on committed usage, with 1.25x overage multiplier. Example: commitment = 1B tokens/mo -> committed price = $0.0144 /1k tokens -> monthly $14,400. If usage = 1.2B, overage billed at 1.25 * committed unit = $0.018 /1k tokens for the 200M overage.
- Enterprise anchor: commit >12 months + capacity buffer -> deeper discount (45–55%) + 2-month free onboarding credits. Always require a minimum quarterly billing cadence.

Concessions ladder (what to give away, and in what order):
1) Free onboarding credits (time-boxed to first 90d), limit to 2x committed avg monthly usage.
2) SRE onboarding hours (up to 20h) for Dedicated/Private customers for integration stretch.
3) Extended support window (24/7) for >$X ARR deals, but tie to an uplift in dollars.
4) Increased SLA uptime % only for 24+ month commitments; otherwise offer operational playbooks and runbooks.
5) Avoid: permanent below-cost token rates, unrestricted IP/data residency exceptions, multi-year exclusivity.

Sample scripts by persona:
- Engineering lead (concern: latency & burst): "We can reserve a pool sized for your 95th percentile concurrent usage and include burst capacity controls. If you exceed the committed throughput, overage billing is predictable at 1.25x. That way you get predictable per-token costs for steady usage and a clear path to scale. We can also propose a temporary burst buffer for the first 60 days to smooth onboarding traffic."
- Procurement (concern: pricing floor & credit terms): "Standard cadence is quarterly billing on reserved contracts. We can consider 45-day net payment terms for Enterprise deals over $XXXk MRR with an approved credit check. In exchange, we expect a 12–24 month commitment and a modest uplift in discount sensitivity."
- CTO (risk/regulatory): "For Private deployments, we can scope a statement of work for air-gapped delivery and integrate with your KMS/HSM. For hosted Reserved, we provide SOC2 reports, audit logs, and a private tenancy model (dedicated capacity) with clearly defined data handling terms. We rarely accept unlimited data residency exceptions without premium pricing—this is high-cost to operate."

Fall-back offers (if buyer pushes hard):
- Short-term blended pilots: 3-month pilot at 70% of committed tier pricing with an automatic conversion clause if usage > 75% of pilot capacity for final 30 days.
- Flex-commit: commit to X tokens/mo for 12 months with quarterly reassessment and a cap on overage volatility.
- Capacity swap: allow customers to shift committed GPU pool between models (e.g., cheaper quantized variants) once per year with a 30d notice, provided performance regressions are evaluated by Redwood.

SLA / credits language (talk points):
- Target P99 latency SLOs are model-dependent; use runtime benchmarks in the deal annex.
- Uptime SLA: standard 99.5% for Dedicated. For better uptime (99.9%) require 24+ month commitment and technical review.
- Credits: 5% monthly credit for single-month SLA misses, 15% for repeated misses (max 35% in a 12-month period). Always subject to force majeure exceptions.

Non-starters / legal redlines to push back on:
- Unlimited indemnity/penalty clauses tied to model outputs.
- Open-ended SLAs on latency for unbounded sequence lengths.
- Permanent price guarantees for new model families (we commit to grandfathered pricing on pinned model versions only for the contract duration).

Playbook for SE during negotiation call (step-by-step):
1) Discovery: ask traffic shape (peak qps, 95th pct usage, sequence length distribution), current spend, and tolerance for burst.
2) Anchor: present committed tiers and show three scenario math (conservative, baseline, aggressive) with monthly $ impact.
3) Objection handling: use scripts above.
4) Offer concession ladder item 1 only; ask for a written LOI with basic sizes.
5) Close: get buy-in on timeline, technical kickoff, and who owns billing/legal contacts.

Sample objections & counters: 
- "We can't commit to months up front": "Let's run a 90-day pilot with an auto-convert clause if you hit >80% of pilots' average committed throughput in the last 30d."
- "We need better price floor": "We can do a deeper discount for a 24+ month term, but we'll require a minimum quarterly billing guarantee and a model pin on production variants."
- "Latency SLA must be 99.99%": "For 99.99% on general-purpose models we'd need a dedicated SRE engagement and a premium; propose 99.9% with a technical deep-dive to scope improvements and a 12mo review clause."

Deal examples (faux numbers for internal training):
- SMB: commit 200M tokens/mo for 12 months -> 30% discount, monthly bill $2,880. Onboarding credit: 1 month free runtime.
- Mid-market: commit 1B tokens/mo for 12 months -> 40% discount, monthly bill $14,400. Limited SRE hours included.
- Enterprise: commit 5B tokens/mo for 24 months -> 50% discount, 2-month onboarding credit, 24/7 premium support, 30-day migration support to Private if needed.

Negotiation pitfalls we've seen (tactical notes):
- Customers ask for open-data residency clauses late; escalate early to Legal & Solutions.
- Procurement anchors on list price too often; re-anchor with unit economics and ARR impact.
- Sales gives deep price and also long credit terms without legal sign-off—avoid unless Sales Ops approves.

Deck checklist for AE/SE to share during commercial review:
- Include usage shape chart, model family, latency SLOs, preferred termination clause, price tier table, onboarding plan timeline, and a clear acceptance definition. Convert to a one-page annex for the contract.

Open items & TO-DOs: 
- Get legal-approved SLA credit caps for Private deployments (Owner: Claire Wong, JIRA-OPS-1783).
- Create a templated Annex A (usage + pinning + performance test) (Owner: Ravi Shah).
- Add real unit costs by model family to pricing calculator (Owner: Finance).

Notes to self / rough ideas: 
- Consider a "peak smoothing" product: customer pays a small monthly premium to have 1.2x burst cushion automatically applied without overage shocks. Could improve close rates on midmarket.
- Track how many deals ask for model pinning vs. general price guarantees. Could be a product tier.

References & links:

- Sales tools: pricing calculator (internal app).
- Example redlined T&Cs: github.com/redwood-inference/contracts/examples.
